## Why? {#why}

**Research question:** How satisfied were the participants of the remote study with the app?

The responses come as an export from the survey tool, once as CSV and once as an Excel file. Neither looks like a clean table: info lines above the header, a second header row with the question text, decimal commas, `-99` for "no answer", a totals row. If you read this carelessly, you later compute with wrong numbers, often without any error message.

## Concept {#concept}

Reading a file means telling R four things about it:

```{=html}
<figure class="rt-figure">
<svg viewBox="0 0 560 190" role="img" aria-labelledby="fig-imp-title fig-imp-desc" xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg">
  <title id="fig-imp-title">Structure of the CSV export</title>
  <desc id="fig-imp-desc">Lines 1 to 3 are export info and are skipped, line 4 is the header with the column names, line 5 the question text, from line 6 on follow the responses with semicolon as delimiter and comma as decimal mark.</desc>
  <rect x="20" y="10" width="330" height="44" rx="4" class="rt-fig-box" />
  <text x="32" y="28" class="rt-fig-code rt-fig-muted">Survey export: App feedback …</text>
  <text x="32" y="46" class="rt-fig-code rt-fig-muted">Exported: 2026-03-24 …</text>
  <rect x="20" y="62" width="330" height="24" rx="4" class="rt-fig-box-accent" />
  <text x="32" y="79" class="rt-fig-code">"Response ID";"Start Date";…</text>
  <rect x="20" y="94" width="330" height="24" rx="4" class="rt-fig-box" />
  <text x="32" y="111" class="rt-fig-code rt-fig-muted">"Response ID";"How old are…</text>
  <rect x="20" y="126" width="330" height="52" rx="4" class="rt-fig-box-accent" />
  <text x="32" y="144" class="rt-fig-code">"R_0001";…;"308,0";…</text>
  <text x="32" y="166" class="rt-fig-code">"R_0002";…;"-99";…</text>
  <text x="365" y="37" class="rt-fig-label">skip (lines 1–3)</text>
  <text x="365" y="79" class="rt-fig-label">column names</text>
  <text x="365" y="111" class="rt-fig-label">question text: skip</text>
  <text x="365" y="144" class="rt-fig-label">delim = ";"</text>
  <text x="365" y="166" class="rt-fig-label">decimal_mark, na</text>
</svg>
<figcaption>Look at the file first, then specify the delimiter, lines to skip, number format and missing-value codes.</figcaption>
</figure>
```

- **Delimiter (`delim`):** `;` in German and many other European exports, because the comma is the decimal mark.
- **Skip lines (`skip`), limit length (`n_max`):** for info lines at the top and totals rows at the bottom.
- **Number format (`locale`):** `locale(decimal_mark = ",")`. Without it, `308,0` silently becomes 3080.
- **Missing-value codes (`na`):** `-99`, `n/a` or `999` are valid values for R until you declare them missing.
- **Check afterwards:** types (`<dbl>`, `<chr>`, `<lgl>`), number of rows, value ranges. A text column where numbers should be almost always points to a problem in the data.

## Example {#example}

Before reading, look at the raw file line by line:

```{webr}
readLines(raw_export_csv, n = 6)
```

Then read it. The column names are in line 4, the responses start in line 6:

```{webr}
header <- read_delim(raw_export_csv, delim = ";", skip = 3, n_max = 0, show_col_types = FALSE)
raw <- read_delim(
  raw_export_csv,
  delim = ";",
  skip = 5,
  col_names = names(header),
  locale = locale(decimal_mark = ","),
  na = c("", "NA", "n/a", "-99"),
  show_col_types = FALSE
)
raw
```

Which types did readr detect? `spec()` shows them; text columns (`col_character()`) containing numbers are candidates for cleaning:

```{webr}
spec(raw)
```

The same responses from Excel. `excel_sheets()` lists the sheets, `range` sets the table area, `clean_names()` makes the names R-friendly:

```{webr}
excel_sheets(raw_export_xlsx)
read_excel(raw_export_xlsx, sheet = "Export", range = "A4:N86") |>
  clean_names()
```

**How to report it (methods section):** Of 82 exported records, 2 were test responses and 2 were duplicate submissions; 78 responses were analysed. Missing-value codes (`-99`) were treated as missing. (Removing them follows in the lesson "Cleaning data".)

## Package comparison {#packages}

| Approach | Strength | When |
|---|---|---|
| `readr::read_delim()` / `read_csv()` / `read_csv2()` | Fast, no automatic factors, reports types and problems (`problems()`) | **Recommended** for CSV and text |
| `utils::read.csv()` / `read.csv2()` | No packages; common in older code | When no packages are allowed; column names get changed (`Response.ID`) |
| `readxl::read_excel()` | Reads `.xls` and `.xlsx` without Excel, specific ranges and sheets | **Recommended** for Excel |
| `haven::read_sav()` | SPSS files with value labels (Qualtrics, LimeSurvey, SoSci Survey) | When the tool exports SPSS: labels are kept |

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## Run locally

In the browser the files are already in place. Locally, you read from the project folder, e.g. `read_delim("data/raw_export.csv", ...)`. For SPSS exports:

```r
survey <- haven::read_sav("data/export.sav")
haven::as_factor(survey)   # value labels as factor levels
```
:::

## Cheat sheet {#cheatsheet}

```r
# Look first
readLines("data/raw_export.csv", n = 6)

# CSV with ; and decimal comma, info lines and missing-value codes
header <- read_delim(file, delim = ";", skip = 3, n_max = 0)
raw <- read_delim(file, delim = ";", skip = 5, col_names = names(header),
                  locale = locale(decimal_mark = ","), na = c("", "NA", "-99"))

# Excel: sheet and range
read_excel(file, sheet = "Export", range = "A4:N86") |> janitor::clean_names()

# Check afterwards
spec(raw); problems(raw); nrow(raw); tail(raw)
```

- Decimal comma → `locale(decimal_mark = ",")` or `read_csv2()`.
- Declare missing-value codes when reading with `na = ...` (keep the defaults `""` and `"NA"`).
- After reading, always check types, number of rows and the end of the table.
